questions.skill: Show that replacing an equation by its sum with a multiple of the other keeps the solutions of a system
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: System: x + y = 7 and x - y = 1. Replace the second equation by the sum of the two equations. Write the new system, solve it, and show that the solution also satisfies the original system.
questions.prompt_markup:
System: x + y = 7 and x - y = 1.
Replace the second equation by the sum of the two equations. Write the new system, solve it, and show that the solution also satisfies the original system.
questions.required_method: The new system x + y = 7 and 2x = 8, its solution, and a check of the solution in both original equations.
questions.grading_note: Form required: the new system, the solution, and the check. 2x = 8 gives x = 4, so y = 3. Check: 4 + 3 = 7 and 4 - 3 = 1.

questions.skill: Show that replacing an equation by its sum with a multiple of the other keeps the solutions of a system
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Suppose (a, b) is a solution of the system 2x + y = 5 and x - 3y = 6. Explain why (a, b) is also a solution of (2x + y) + 2(x - 3y) = 5 + 2(6).
questions.prompt_markup:
Suppose (a, b) is a solution of the system 2x + y = 5 and x - 3y = 6.
Explain why (a, b) is also a solution of (2x + y) + 2(x - 3y) = 5 + 2(6).
questions.correct_answer: Since 2a + b = 5 and a - 3b = 6, 2(a - 3b) = 12. Adding equal amounts to both sides of 2a + b = 5 gives (2a + b) + 2(a - 3b) = 5 + 12, a true equation.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent explanation that substitutes (a, b) and adds equal quantities to both sides.

questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: System: 3x + 2y = 12 and x - y = -1. Which system has the same solution?
questions.prompt_markup:
System: 3x + 2y = 12 and x - y = -1.
Which system has the same solution?
questions.grading_note: Adding the first equation and 2 times the second gives 5x = 10. The solution of both systems is (2, 3); (2, 3) does not satisfy 5x = 14, 4x + y = 13, or 2x + 3y = 11.

questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Replacing one equation of a system by the sum of that equation and 3 times the other equation can change the solutions of the system.
questions.prompt_markup: Replacing one equation of a system by the sum of that equation and 3 times the other equation can change the solutions of the system.
questions.grading_note: Any solution of the old system satisfies the new equation, and the old equation can be recovered by subtracting 3 times the other, so the solutions stay the same.

questions.skill: Show that replacing an equation by its sum with a multiple of the other keeps the solutions of a system
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: In the system 2x + 3y = 7 and 4x - 3y = 5, adding the equations eliminates y and gives 6x = 12.
questions.prompt_markup: In the system 2x + 3y = 7 and 4x - 3y = 5, adding the equations eliminates y and gives 6x = 12.
questions.grading_note: 3y + (-3y) = 0 and 7 + 5 = 12. Then x = 2 and y = 1.

questions.prompt: Write the system 2x + y = 7 and x - 3y = 0 as a matrix equation AX = B. Give A, X, and B.
questions.prompt_markup: Write the system 2x + y = 7 and x - 3y = 0 as a matrix equation AX = B. Give A, X, and B.
questions.correct_answer: A has rows [2 1] and [1 -3]; X is the column [x, y]; B is the column [7, 0]; and AX = B.
questions.grading_note: Form required: A, X, and B, in this order of rows.
